proof.text: Set $\mathcal A_s=\operatorname{Mod}(R_s)$ and $M_K=\mathcal T_a^cK$. The strict-tower functor gives $\operatorname{ev}_nM_K=\operatorname{Res}_nF_nK_n$ naturally, with exactly the quotient-induced compact-support transitions, including every composite transition. By the integral compact-support definition, interpreted on this specified strict tower, $N_K=Ra_!K=R\lim M_K$. Here we use the total-limit functor, not an arbitrary choice of a triangulated Roos cone. Thus its projections are the actual compact-support projections $N_K\to\operatorname{Res}_nF_nK_n$. The same definition of the transitions applies on morphisms because $\mathcal T_a^c$ is a functor.

proof.text: Let $F:\mathcal A_s\to\operatorname{Mod}(R)$ be $\Gamma(s,-)$ followed by restriction along $R\to\Gamma(s,R_s)$. Point sections are exact since $k$ is algebraically closed; restriction changes only the scalar action, so preserves kernels and cokernels. Hence $F$ and its levelwise tower functor are exact. The exact-functor factorization identifies their derived functors with termwise application. In particular the separately derived tower sections in the statement give $B_K=F_D^{\operatorname{Tow}}M_K$, and $\operatorname{ev}_nB_K=C_n$ with the same transitions. No inverse limit is taken by these tower sections.

source.place: Tag 0940, section-derived-limits, tower site; exact point sections and exact derived factorization from the cited nodes.

proof.text:
Countable products in $\mathcal A_s$ are sectionwise and exact by the pro-etale product theorem. In $\operatorname{Mod}(R)$ they are exact too: the kernel of a product map is the product of its kernels, and a family in the product of targets of surjections has a preimage by choosing one preimage in each coordinate. The canonical product comparison for $F$ is the identity $F(\prod_iL_i)=\prod_iF(L_i)$ on sections at $s$, with the restricted $R$-actions. The exact-product-functor strict-limit comparison therefore applies and gives the natural isomorphism
$$\lambda_K:C=F_DN_K=F_D R\lim M_K\xrightarrow{\sim}R\lim F_D^{\operatorname{Tow}}M_K=R\lim B_K.$$
Its stated projection equation says $\pi_n\lambda_K=F_D(N_K\to\operatorname{Res}_nF_nK_n)$. Thus it identifies the specified projections, not merely the two limit objects.

source.place: Tags 0940 and 0941, section-derived-limits and lemma-derived-limit-is-ok; normalized strict-limit comparison as in the cited existing refinement.

proof.text:
On $R$-modules, let $\Delta$ be the constant tower functor and $L$ ordinary inverse limit. The correspondence $h:V\to LT\mapsto(\pi_nh)_n$ identifies module maps into the limit with tower maps $\Delta V\to T$; its inverse sends a compatible family to its map into the limit. These are inverse and natural by their coordinate formulas, so $\Delta\dashv L$. Moreover $\Delta$ is additive and exact because tower exactness is levelwise. Its left derived functor is therefore the same termwise constant functor. The total right derived functor of $L$ exists on every tower by the total-limit theorem. Applying the general derived-adjoint theorem gives
$$\Delta:D(R)\ \dashv\ R\lim:D(\operatorname{Tow}(\operatorname{Mod}(R))).$$

source.place: Tag 09T5, lemma-derived-adjoint-functors; tower projection of sites-cohomology.tex Tag 0940.

proof.text:
Write $\epsilon_B:\Delta R\lim B\to B$ for this derived adjunction's counit. Its normalization can be read on a K-injective tower representative $I$ of $B$: $R\lim B$ is $\lim I$, and the counit is the chain map $\Delta\lim I\to I$ with components $\pi_n$. Indeed the fraction formula for the canonical derived adjunction, taking the identity resolution of the exact left functor and the K-injective resolution for the right functor, sends $1_{\lim I}$ to the ordinary counit with precisely these components. Consequently $\operatorname{ev}_n\epsilon_B$ is the actual total-limit projection, after the resolution identifications. Define
$$\eta_K=\epsilon_{B_K}\circ\Delta(\lambda_K):\Delta C\to B_K.$$
By Step 3 its $n$th evaluation is exactly the compact-support projection $C\to C_n$.

source.place: Tag 0FND, lemma-pre-derived-adjoint-functors-general, fraction characterization; sites-cohomology.tex Tag 0941, K-injective tower model.

proof.text:
For $f:K\to K'$ let $b=B(f)$ and $c=C(f)$. Naturality of the comparison in Step 3 gives $(R\lim b)\lambda_K=\lambda_{K'}c$. Naturality of the derived counit gives $b\epsilon_{B_K}=\epsilon_{B_{K'}}\Delta(R\lim b)$. Substitution yields
$$b\eta_K=\epsilon_{B_{K'}}\Delta(R\lim b)\Delta\lambda_K=\epsilon_{B_{K'}}\Delta\lambda_{K'}\Delta c=\eta_{K'}\Delta c.$$
This equality is in the derived tower category itself. It does not infer equality of tower morphisms from equality of their evaluations.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2, sentence after the displayed calculation asserting that the specified natural maps are identified; elementary counit-naturality calculation.

proof.text:
Apply integral compact-support reduction to $a:X\to s$ and $K$. The base field, $\ell\ne p$, separated finite-type morphism, dimension bound $d\ge0$, and common Tor interval $[a_0,b_0]$ are exactly its hypotheses. It gives $N_K\in D^b_c(s,R)$ and the canonical coherent isomorphism $r_n:N_K\otimes^L_{R_s}(A_n)_s\xrightarrow{\sim}F_nK_n$. Apply point-sections derived reduction to this $N_K$. Composing gives a natural isomorphism
$$\alpha_n:C\otimes_R^LA_n\xrightarrow{\sim}\Gamma(s,N_K\otimes^L_{R_s}(A_n)_s)\xrightarrow{\Gamma(s,r_n)}C_n.$$
The first arrow concerns modules over the completed sheaf on $s$, with scalar restriction to $R$; it is not an identification with the discrete constant integral sheaf.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2, third displayed comparison: integral compact-support reduction and point sections.

proof.text: We specify the unit compatibility of the point-sections comparison rather than assuming it from naturality. Put $t=\varpi^n$ and $A=A_n$. The coefficient DVR is a PID, hence Noetherian since each ideal has one generator. The finite-free resolution $[R\xrightarrow{t}R]\to A$ and the completed-constant reduction theorem identify $[R_s\xrightarrow{t}R_s]$, augmented by the actual coefficient projection, with $(A_n)_s[0]$. Thus $0\to R_s\xrightarrow{t}R_s\to(A_n)_s\to0$ is exact. Apply the resolution-independence comparison for exact sections with $\mathcal O=R_s$, $\mathcal O'=(A_n)_s$ and final object $s$. Its hypotheses are this sequence and exact point sections. On a flat-term K-flat sheaf representative $P$ of $N_K$, it specifies the comparison as $\theta_Pc_{\Gamma P}$, where $c$ is the universal ordinary derived-tensor counit and $\theta_P:\Gamma P/t\Gamma P\to\Gamma(P/tP)$ sends a quotient of a section to its quotient section. These are the normalized quotient maps underlying the point-sections isomorphism in Step 7.

source.place: Tags 093M and 093J, completion and constant-sheaf reduction; sites-cohomology.tex Tag 06YS, K-flat models; explicit normalization of the existing point-sections comparison.

proof.text:
Choose a flat-term K-flat ordinary-module resolution $q:Q\to\Gamma P$ on the one-object trivial site. The counit's naturality gives $c_{\Gamma P}L(q)=\bar q\,c_Q$, where $\bar q:Q/tQ\to\Gamma P/t\Gamma P$ is induced by $q$ and $c_Q$ is the K-flat identification. Thus the comparison in Step 8, on the representative $Q/tQ$, is
$$\bar x\longmapsto\text{the image of }q(x)\text{ in }\Gamma(P/tP).$$
By the normalized scalar adjunction (on the trivial site for modules and on $s_{\mathrm{proet}}$ for sheaves), its adjunct is the class of $Q\to\Gamma(P/tP)$, $x\mapsto q(x)\bmod t$. This is the composite of $q$ with sections of the reduction unit $P\to P/tP$. All comparisons are therefore normalized with the same unit $x\mapsto x\otimes1$; no K-flatness of $\Gamma P$ is needed.

source.place: Tags 06YS and 07A6, K-flat models and scalar adjunction; ordinary derived-tensor counit naturality as in the cited existing comparison.

proof.text: Finally compose that point-sections comparison with $\Gamma(s,r_n)$ from Step 7. Its scalar-extension adjunct is sections of the reduction unit followed by $r_n$, by Step 9. Since $r_n$ is the canonical compact-support coefficient comparison, this composite is the actual compact-support projection $C\to C_n$. That is exactly $\operatorname{ev}_n\eta_K$ by Steps 3 and 5. The scalar adjunction bijection therefore identifies $\alpha_n$ with the adjunct of $\operatorname{ev}_n\eta_K$, proving the last clause, including its specified map.

title: Compact-support tower coaugmentation
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum with $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. Fix a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $R$, a uniformizer $\varpi$, and $A_n=R/\varpi^n$ for $n\ge1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $a:X\to s=\operatorname{Spec}k$ be separated and of finite type [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Use ordinary module sheaves on the small pro-etale sites, with completed coefficient sheaf $R_W=\lim_n(A_n)_W$ for $W=X,s$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Write $F_n=Ra_{!,n}$ for compact support using one fixed compactification $a=pj$ [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support], $G_n=Ra_n^!$ for the finite constructible comparison-class exceptional functor [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], and $\omega_n=G_n(A_n)_s$. Let $K\in D^b_c(X,R)$ [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], let $K_n=K\otimes^L_{R_X}(A_n)_X$ [def-weil-integral-derived-reduction], and suppose its reductions have Tor amplitude in one finite interval $[a_0,b_0]$ [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. Put $C_n=\Gamma(s,F_nK_n)$ and $C=\Gamma(s,Ra_!K)$, with coefficient-point sections [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point]. Suppose $\dim X\le d$ for an integer $d\ge0$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Let $\mathcal T_a^cK$ be the specified strict compact-support reduction tower [lem-weil-compact-support-reduction-tower-functor] and put $B_K=R\Gamma^{\operatorname{Tow}}(s,\mathcal T_a^cK)$, with scalars restricted to $R$. Use total derived inverse limits and derived tower categories as in [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]. There is a natural isomorphism $C\cong R\lim B_K$ compatible with all finite projections, and the derived constant/limit counit gives a natural morphism
$$\eta_K:\operatorname{const}C\longrightarrow B_K$$
in $D(\operatorname{Tow}(\operatorname{Mod}(R)))$. Under $\operatorname{ev}_nB_K\cong C_n$, its evaluation is the actual compact-support projection $C\to C_n$. The scalar-extension adjunct of this evaluation is the canonical isomorphism $C\otimes_R^LA_n\xrightarrow{\sim}C_n$ of [lem-pod-point-sections-derived-reduction] and [lem-coef-integral-compact-support].
